Name: HD Core
Author: ParadoxQED
Description:
[size=4][b]Description[/b][/size]

HDCore is a small framework that lets item icons in Stardew Valley use their [b]full texture resolution[/b] without changing how much space they take on screen.
Vanilla always draws an item icon from a hard-coded 16×16 slice of its texture and then scales that slice up 4×. A 64×64 texture therefore only ever shows its top-left corner. HDCore changes that single path: it samples the [b]whole texture[/b] for qualifying items, then scales it by "64 / texture size", so the icon still occupies exactly one 64px grid cell.
Version 2.0 also handles [b]tilesheets[/b]: a mod can declare the cell size of an atlas, and each item then draws the one cell its "SpriteIndex" points at — still into the same 64px cell. Cell size must be declared, never guessed: a 256×256 sheet can be 16px cells or 64px cells, and guessing wrong would squash the whole atlas into a single icon. Undeclared atlases keep vanilla slicing, exactly as before. Cells are indexed row-major, and index "0" is reserved for whole-image icons — atlas entries should start at "1".
Version 2.1 adds [b]non-square art[/b]. A mod can declare a texture as padded: at load time the image is centred and its canvas extended on the short axis until it is square ("side = max(width, height)"), and from then on it travels the exact same square path. No pixel is resampled and no draw formula was added — the canvas simply becomes square before the existing code sees it, which is why the change cannot alter how anything already working is drawn.
The result: 16×16 art looks identical to vanilla, 64×64 art is four times sharper, and both can sit side by side without one looking blurry next to the other.
HDCore does [b]not[/b] modify asset files on disk, and nothing is taken over unless a mod declares it. The only load-time edits are in memory, for textures that mod explicitly registered: square images above 1024px are area-averaged down to 1024, and non-square images opted into padding get their canvas squared. Anything not registered renders exactly like vanilla.
Who it is for:
[list]
[*][b]Players[/b] — install it and forget it. There is no config and no in-game menu. Mods that support HD icons simply look sharper.[/*]
[/list][list]
[*][b]Mod authors[/b] — a short registration gets your high-resolution icons displayed properly in inventories, shops, crafting menus and on the ground.[/*]
[/list]

[size=4][b]Installation instructions[/b][/size]
[list=1]
[*][color=#d4d4d8]Install SMAPI 4.0.0 or later.[/color][/*]
[*][color=#D4D4D8]Download and unzip HDCore.[/color][/*]
[*][color=#d4d4d8]Put the "[/color]HDCore" folder into your "Stardew Valley/Mods" folder.[/*]
[*][color=#d4d4d8]Launch the game through SMAPI.[/color][/*]
[/list]To confirm it loaded, check your SMAPI log for a line containing "[HDCore]".
To uninstall, delete the "HDCore" folder. Mods that relied on it fall back to vanilla rendering automatically, and no save data is touched.


[size=4][b]Main features[/b][/size]
[list]
[*][b]Full-resolution icons, same footprint[/b] — qualifying textures are drawn from the whole image and scaled to a fixed 64px cell, so grid layout never changes.[/*]
[/list][list]
[*][b]Tilesheets (2.0)[/b] — declare an atlas and its cell size via "RegisterSheets", and each item draws the cell its "SpriteIndex" points at. Cell size is always declared, never inferred; undeclared atlases are untouched.[/*]
[/list][list]
[*][b]Optional 17–63 support (2.0)[/b] — by default only square textures of 64px and up are taken over. A mod can opt in to smaller ones with "RegisterWithMinSize(..., 17)": the icon then shows its [b]complete[/b] art instead of the top-left 16×16. Note this is an upscale band — the picture becomes whole, not sharper.[/*]
[/list][list]
[*][b]Non-square art (2.1)[/b] — a mod can opt in with "RegisterPadded". The texture is centred and its canvas squared at load (no resampling), then handled like any other square icon, so portrait-shaped art no longer renders as just its top-left corner. Skipped for atlases, for sheets that several items share through "SpriteIndex", and for anything absurdly large.[/*]
[/list][list]
[*][b]One consistent path everywhere[/b] — inventory, shops, crafting menu, BetterCrafting recipe grid, buff icons, held items and dropped-item debris all use the same scaling rule, so HD icons no longer become 4× giants in the world.[/*]
[/list][list]
[*][b]Furniture icons[/b] — non-square furniture art is fitted by its longest edge to 64px instead of overflowing its cell.[/*]
[/list][list]
[*][b]Weapons[/b] — weapon textures keep a downscaled copy for the 4× held/swing path (so a held weapon stays normal-sized) while the full-resolution original is used for menu icons.[/*]
[/list][list]
[*][b]Big craftables[/b] — square big-craftable icons are drawn as a one-cell-wide square anchored to the bottom of their footprint, instead of being stretched to twice their height by the vanilla 1:2 target rectangle.[/*]
[/list][list]
[*][b]Large-texture handling[/b] — only square item textures larger than 1024×1024 are area-averaged down to 1024 at load time; anything smaller is kept native.[/*]
[/list][list]
[*][b]Opt-in by design[/b] — unregistered mods, [i]undeclared[/i] multi-frame atlases ("SpriteIndex != 0"), 16×16 legacy art and UI textures are never touched.[/*]
[/list][list]
[*][b]Fail-safe patches[/b] — every patch is wrapped individually, so a single failed hook disables only that path and never interrupts the game.[/*]
[/list]

[size=4][b]Requirements[/b][/size]
[list]
[*][color=#D4D4D8][b]Stardew Valley 1.6+[/b][/color][/*]
[/list][list]
[*][color=#D4D4D8][b]SMAPI 4.0.0+[/b] (required)[/color][/*]
[/list][list]
[*][color=#D4D4D8][b]BetterCrafting[/b] (optional) — detected at runtime, its recipe grid is scaled automatically. HDCore never references its assembly directly.[/color][/*]
[/list]

[size=4][b]For mod authors[/b][/size]
HDCore is a framework; nothing is taken over automatically. To have your icons handled:
[list=1]
[*]Declare the dependency in your "manifest.json". Pick the minimum version that matches the API you actually call: 
"Dependencies": [  { "UniqueID": "ParadoxQED.HDCore", "MinimumVersion": "1.0.0", "IsRequired": true }]
Do not declare a lower version than the methods you use — SMAPI's API proxy resolves members by name, so calling "RegisterSheets" against a 1.x build fails at runtime instead of at load.[/*]
[*]Declare a matching interface in your own source. You do not need to reference "HDCore.dll" — SMAPI proxies the API by member name: 
public interface IHdCoreApi{    bool IsApplied { get; }    int IconSize { get; }    int IndexedTextures { get; }    bool Register(string modUniqueId, string[] textureNamePatterns);}[/*]
[*]Register from "GameLaunched" — querying the API earlier returns null: 
var api = Helper.ModRegistry.GetApi<IHdCoreApi>("ParadoxQED.HDCore");api?.Register(ModManifest.UniqueID, new[] { "Mods/YourAuthor.YourMod/" });[/*]
[/list]Registration is rejected when the dependency is not declared in your manifest, and methods are deliberately [b]not[/b] overloaded — SMAPI's API proxy maps by method name, so distinct names avoid ambiguity. Author your icons as [b]square and at least 64×64[/b] (68, 72, 96, 128 all work — they are scaled by actual size). If the source art is rectangular, either pad the short edge up to the long one in the PNG, or leave the PNG alone and call "RegisterPadded" — never stretch it. Don't use "RegisterPadded" on furniture textures that are also drawn in the world: vanilla slices those with its own source rectangles, so a shifted canvas would misalign them.


[size=4][b]Shout outs[/b][/size]
[list]
[*]The Stardew Valley modding community and the SMAPI team, for an API that makes this kind of surgical draw-path change possible.[/*]
[/list][list]
[*]Everyone who reported blurry or oversized icons — those reports shaped the 1.1.0 and 1.2.0 fixes, and the 2.x work that followed.[/*]
[/list]

Manifest.Name: HD 图标引擎 (HDCore)
Manifest.Description: 高清物品图标引擎：贴图整图取样 + 屏幕上恒定 64px + 制作界面（含 BetterCrafting）同步缩放。默认只对「方形、边长 ≥64、SpriteIndex = 0」的物品贴图生效；2.0 起支持两类新口径——（1）RegisterWithMinSize 可把下限降到 17，让 17~63 的方形素材也完整显示（放大档，像素密度不变）；（2）RegisterSheets 声明图集格子边长，按 SpriteIndex 取格子绘制（格子尺寸必须显式声明，绝不推断）。2.1 起 RegisterPadded 支持非方形素材：加载期把短边居中、两边扩画布补成正方形，之后按方形口径接管（同样必须显式声明）。1.2.0：修正建造物世界绘制的 1:2 拉伸。1.2.1：加载降采样阈值 256 → 1024。
Manifest.Author: ParadoxQED
